chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The basis of the will is that the man frees whom he wishes, confirms whom he wishes, acquires slavery for whom he freed, and frees whom he acquired slavery for.
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for freeing and confirming slaves in a Islamic will according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Reported by Shaykh al-Tusi in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the foundational principle of testamentary freedom regarding slaves, allowing the owner to selectively manumit or retain servitude. It introduces a reciprocal legal mechanism where freeing a slave permits acquiring a new one, and retaining a slave allows for the manumission of another, reflecting the dynamic nature of property disposition in early Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the owner's absolute discretion (*ikhtiyar*) in managing his slaves as part of his estate, a key concept in the chapter on revoking or modifying wills.
